title: Reading a simple budget
examples: Teacher, how do I know if I have enough money?
What is the difference between profit and income?
Can you show us a real example of a budget?

explain.say: Today we are learning about simple budgets. A budget helps us plan our money use. We will look at income, expenses, profit, and loss.
Income is the money you receive over a certain time. This is the money coming in. For example, if you earn pocket money, that is your income.
Expenses are the costs of things you buy or use. These are the money going out. For example, buying a snack at the school canteen is an expense.
Profit happens when your income is more than your expenses. You have extra money left over. For example, if you earn ten dollars and spend six dollars, you have a profit.
A loss happens when your expenses are more than your income. You have spent more money than you earned. For example, if you only earn five dollars but spend eight dollars, you have a loss.
In real life, you use budgets for many things. Think about planning a school trip. Your income might be the money you save. Your expenses include tickets and food.

draw.text: Real Life: Planning a Trip Budget

faq.q: What is the main difference between profit and income?
faq.a: Income is all the money you bring in. Profit is what you have left after paying all your costs.
asks: What is the difference between money earned and money left?
Is profit the same thing as income?

faq.q: If I have a loss, does that mean I have no money?
faq.a: No, it means your spending was higher than your income for that period. You might need to earn more next time.
asks: What does it mean to have a negative budget?
Can I still have money if I have a loss?

faq.q: Do I have to track every single penny to budget well?
faq.a: It is best to track everything to be accurate. For simple budgets, tracking big items is a good start.
asks: How detailed should my budget be?

faq.q: Can a business have a profit and a loss in the same month?
faq.a: Generally, a business reports one result for a period. If they lose money one month, they aim for a profit the next.
asks: Can I switch between profit and loss?
Does the result change month to month?

faq.q: What is the first thing I should do when making a budget?
faq.a: The first step is to calculate all your expected income. Knowing your income sets the limit for your spending.
asks: Where do I start with budgeting?
What is the first number I need for a budget?

facts: Income is money received, like wages or gifts.
Expenses are costs paid out, like rent or food.
Profit occurs when income exceeds expenses.
A loss happens when expenses are greater than income.

quiz.say: If you earn forty dollars and spend twenty dollars, what is your result?
quiz.why: You subtract your expenses from your income to find the remaining profit.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you added the two numbers together.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you only calculated the difference, not the total.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only used the income amount.

quiz.say: A student buys a book for twelve dollars but only has ten dollars. What is the result?
quiz.why: Since spending is more than earning, the difference is a loss.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you added the two amounts together.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you subtracted the smaller number from the larger one incorrectly.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you ignored the extra money needed.

quiz.say: If a small shop sells items for one hundred dollars and spends sixty dollars on supplies, what is the profit?
quiz.why: Profit is calculated by taking total sales and subtracting the costs of supplies.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you only stated the expenses.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you added the sales and the supplies.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the question asks for the dollar amount, not a percentage.
